name: proxy_diag
description:
Diagnose why a LAN client behind an OpenClash fake-ip bypass router cannot
reach a blocked site (e.g. Chrome cannot open YouTube). It is a first-fail
walk over four probes, in the order a real diagnosis runs them:
1. dns_probe      -- what the client's resolver returned for the blocked
domain: fake-ip (198.18.0.0/16) / poisoned / real-ip /
no answer.
2. gateway_probe  -- is the client default gateway the OpenClash box itself?
fake-ip only gets intercepted when traffic traverses it.
3. intercept_probe-- does the clash log show this client's connections?
(proof the nft redirect/tproxy actually applied).
4. proxy_probe    -- end-to-end via the proxy port: reachable, auth, or
upstream node dead.
The harness (the agent doing the diagnosis) fills four evidence fields before
each call; the graph reads nothing else:
- ev_dns       what the client's resolver returned for the blocked domain,
as a classification plus the raw answer, e.g.
"fake-ip 198.18.0.23", "poisoned 104.244.42.197",
"real-ip 142.250.x.x" or "timeout". Distinguishing GFW
poisoning from a plain real IP needs the diagnosing agent's
judgement, so it carries its own label; the raw IP alone
falls back to real_ip (the safe reading for a non-fake-ip
answer).
- ev_gateway   the client's default gateway, e.g. "192.168.2.1 main router"
or "192.168.2.249 openclash box".
- ev_intercept whether /tmp/openclash.log shows this client IP at all,
e.g. "no client traffic seen" or "saw 192.168.2.83 youtube".
- ev_proxy     the curl result through the proxy port, e.g. "200 ok",
"407 auth required", "refused", "node timeout".
The first probe that fails ends the walk and names the fix:
FIX_DNS / FIX_GATEWAY / FIX_INTERCEPT / FIX_PROXY_AUTH / FIX_PROXY_PORT /
FIX_NODE; a run that clears every probe reaches ALL_GOOD.

dns_state.instructions: What did the client's resolver return for the blocked domain? fake-ip means OpenClash's DNS took over; poisoned or real-ip means it did not; no answer means DNS itself is broken.

criteria.fake_ip: A 198.18.0.0/16 fake-ip address: OpenClash DNS is serving this client.
criteria.poisoned: A wrong real-looking IP (GFW DNS poisoning): DNS bypassed OpenClash.
criteria.real_ip: The real blocked-site IP: DNS bypassed OpenClash entirely.
criteria.no_answer: No response or timeout: DNS is broken for this client.

gateway_state.instructions: Is the client's default gateway the OpenClash bypass router itself? fake-ip addresses are only intercepted by OpenClash's nftables when traffic routes through that box; a gateway pointing at the main router sends fake-ip packets straight into the internet blackhole.

criteria.openclash: The default gateway is the OpenClash box, so fake-ip can be intercepted.
criteria.main_router: The default gateway is the main/ISP router: fake-ip traffic bypasses OpenClash. The single most common fake-ip misconfiguration.
criteria.unknown: The gateway cannot be determined from the evidence.

intercept_state.instructions: Does the OpenClash log show any connection from this client IP? fake-ip being returned plus a correct gateway should produce visible client connections; their absence means the nft redirect/tproxy rules are not applying.

criteria.yes: The clash log lists this client IP (traffic is being intercepted).
criteria.no: The clash log only shows the router's own IP: interception is not happening.

proxy_state.instructions: End-to-end result of fetching the blocked site through the proxy port? Distinguishes a healthy proxy, an auth requirement on the port, a dead port, and a dead upstream node.

criteria.ok: The proxy port served the blocked site (HTTP 200): the whole chain works.
criteria.auth_required: The port answers but demands authentication (407).
criteria.port_down: The port refuses connections or times out.
criteria.node_down: The port works but the upstream node fails the fetch.
